entry.title: Schiansky et al. 2023 SI Note 3
entry.subtitle: schiansky_payment_2023 · P. Schiansky et al. Demonstration of quantum-digital payments. Nature Communications 14, 3849 (2023). doi:10.1038/s41467-023-39519-w
entry.summary: p_d <= exp(-(delta_d^2/2) * (1/2)(1 - p_m/2) * N) [SI Eq. 22] 1 - p_h <= exp(-(delta_h^2/3) * M(e_h,l_h) * N), M = (4+2 sqrt 2) e + l [SI Eqs. 18-20] admissible iff (1/2)(1 - p_m/2)(1 - delta_d) >= M(e_h,l_h)(1 + delta_h) [SI Eq. 23]
entry.anchor: Schiansky 2023 SI Eq. (22) (with Eq. (18) fit); Schiansky 2023 SI Eqs. (19)-(20)

fields.label: Source and theorem
fields.text: Schiansky et al. 2023 SI Note 3: N=1 SDP (Eqs. 14-15), analytic fit of the secure-region boundary (Eqs. 16-18), finite-N Chernoff bounds for honest (Eqs. 19-21) and dishonest (Eqs. 22-23) success; main text Fig. 4b.

fields.label: Assumptions
items: Two merchants (one committed bit per sub-token); TTP honest; i.t.-secure MAC; Client's choice of merchant independent of external bias.
Source emits states diagonal in photon number (SPDC; sigma_k of SI Note 3A with p0, p1, pm); multiphoton probability pm known.
Attack model: general CPTP map on the token producing two classical cryptograms; TTP checks declared error e and loss l.
N -> infinity: exponential de Finetti argument stated informally (SI Note 3B), i.e. collective attacks assumed asymptotically i.i.d.
Finite N: Chernoff-Hoeffding (SI Eqs. 7-8) applied to the mishap count M(e,l) = (4+2 sqrt 2) e + l.

fields.label: Finite n or asymptotic
fields.text: finite N via Chernoff, on top of an asymptotic (de Finetti) reduction

fields.label: Parameters
fields.text:
N: quantum states per committed bit (sub-token length)
p_m: multiphoton emission probability
e_h: honest error rate
l_h: honest loss rate
delta_d: dishonest tolerance (0,1]
delta_h: honest tolerance (0,1]

fields.label: Quantifier over adversaries
fields.text: a malicious Client/Merchant applying any CPTP map to the token (SDP over Choi matrices, N=1), extended to N by an informal de Finetti argument

fields.label: Mathematical bound
fields.text:
p_d <= exp(-(delta_d^2/2) * (1/2)(1 - p_m/2) * N)                         [SI Eq. 22]
1 - p_h <= exp(-(delta_h^2/3) * M(e_h,l_h) * N), M = (4+2 sqrt 2) e + l   [SI Eqs. 18-20]
admissible iff (1/2)(1 - p_m/2)(1 - delta_d) >= M(e_h,l_h)(1 + delta_h)  [SI Eq. 23]

fields.label: Numerical method
fields.text: log space; reproduces p_d = 5.9e-45 at N=4.2e6, p_m=0.0602, delta_d=0.01

fields.label: Independent crosscheck
fields.text: qmint/proofs/checker.py re-derives the numbers but REFUSES to certify (see caveats)

fields.label: Caveats
items: Secure-region boundary Eq. (16) is described by the authors as an analytic expression that FITS the numerical SDP optimum, not a proven closed form.
The N->infinity step is an informal appeal to exponential de Finetti without finite-N correction terms.
Chernoff bound (stated for sums of Bernoulli variables) is applied to the weighted mishap combination M(e,l).
p_d excludes the MAC tag-forgery probability p_t = 1/sqrt|C|; the paper chooses p_d ~ p_t but states no composed epsilon. QMint does not compose them.

Main text vs SI disagree: multiphoton probability 6.76 +- 0.12 % (main; reproduces main-text e_d = 3.79 %) vs p_m = 6.02 +- 0.28 % (SI Table 2; reproduces e_d = 3.82 % and allowed mishaps 0.4849); sub-token length N = 4.2e6 (Fig. 4b) vs 4,482,440 (SI Table 2). The published p_d = 5.911e-45 reproduces ONLY with N = 4.2e6 and p_m = 6.02 % (N = 4,482,440 gives 6.3e-48; p_m = 6.76 % gives 8.7e-45). Cross-checked with lane A (research/THEOREM_REGISTRY_SEED.yaml T-SCH23-FINITE).

OPEN QUESTION (QMint assessment, not a claim of error): SI Eqs. (7)-(8) are multiplicative Chernoff bounds for sums of independent variables in {0,1}. The mishap variable per state takes values in {0, 1, 4+2 sqrt 2} (weight > 1 on errors), outside that hypothesis. Rescaling to [0,1] (divide by w = 4+2 sqrt 2) gives the textbook-valid exponent reduced by w: p_d <= exp(-(delta_d^2/2)(1/2)(1-p_m/2) N / w) = 3.3e-7 at the published tuple instead of 5.9e-45. The authors may have a different justification; until resolved D1 stays uncertifiable. Same issue for the honest bound (Eq. 19).
Therefore results carry evidence kind PUBLISHED_AGGREGATE and status NUMERICALLY_SUPPORTED; the independent checker never marks a D1 certificate CERTIFIED.

fields.label: Reproduced examples
items: p_d = 5.911e-45 (SI Table 2) at N = 4.2e6, p_m = 0.0602, delta_d = 0.01 (ours 5.911e-45); with SI N = 4,482,440 the same formula gives 6.3e-48, so the published number uses N = 4.2e6
e_d(l_m = 0.224) = 3.82 % with p_m = 6.02 % (SI) and 3.79 % with p_m = 6.76 % (main text)
Eq. (23) admissible at delta_h = 0.031, delta_d = 0.01

fields.label: Bounds
fields.text:
- bound_id: P-D1/unf
  axis: epsilon_unf
  anchor: Schiansky 2023 SI Eq. (22) (with Eq. (18) fit)
  formula: exp(-(delta_d^2/2)(1/2)(1-p_m/2) N)
  domain: 0 < delta_d <= 1; 0 <= p_m < 1; Eq. (23) holds; two merchants
  monotonicity:
    p_m: increasing
  domain_only:
  - e_h
  - l_h
- bound_id: P-D1/cor
  axis: epsilon_cor
  anchor: Schiansky 2023 SI Eqs. (19)-(20)
  formula: exp(-(delta_h^2/3) M(e_h,l_h) N)
  domain: 0 < delta_h <= 1; M(e_h,l_h) > 0; Eq. (23) holds
  monotonicity:
    e_h: decreasing
    l_h: decreasing
  domain_only:
  - p_m
